methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.skip_reason: insufficient narrow peer set in Chips & Semiconductors (found 0 same-stage, 0 adjacent-stage, 0 similar-tier; need ≥3)
methods.rationale: 11 same-sector peers exist in Chips & Semiconductors, but none of the narrow filters (same-stage / adjacent-stage / similar-valuation-tier) yielded ≥3 datapoints. Falling back to all-sector median would be misleading.

data.narrative:
Ranovus is a Series D+ stage semiconductor company founded by Hamid Arabzadeh that has raised $236M to date, inclusive of a $36M government grant in August 2025. The broader Chips & Semiconductors sector comprises 11 private peers and 3 public comparables (ALAB, NVDA, AMD), though the company operates in a specialized frontier segment where direct comparability is limited.

Peer-median valuation methodology is not applicable here. The analysis identified zero same-stage peers, zero adjacent-stage peers, and zero similar-tier private companies within the semiconductor sector that would satisfy the minimum three-datapoint threshold for statistical reliability. While private peer reference points exist—including Cerebras, SambaNova Systems, PsiQuantum, Etched, and Tenstorrent—none of these firms occupy sufficiently comparable positions in stage, business model, or capital structure to anchor a credible median multiple. Using an all-sector median would conflate heterogeneous business models and risk material misvaluation.

The inability to triangulate via peer-median reflects the frontier nature of Ranovus's technology segment within semiconductors. Without sufficient same-stage or tier-matched comparables, traditional VC valuation frameworks face a data constraint rather than a methodological failure. A complete valuation would require either expanded dataset collection, reliance on alternative methods (discounted cash flow, venture capital method), or explicit articulation of the valuation ranges implied by public semiconductor benchmarks adjusted for stage and technology risk—none of which are supported by the provided data. The $236M capital raise serves as a floor reflecting investor confidence but does not directly imply post-money valuation.
